title: Quasi-coherent modules on qcqs spaces are filtered colimits of finitely presented modules
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the small etale site and quasi-coherence of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Assume $|X|$ is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover, with topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]) and that its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests. A module is of finite presentation if etale locally it is the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O^{m}\to\mathcal O^{n}$ with $m,n$ finite. For every quasi-coherent module $\mathcal M$ there are a small filtered category $J$, a diagram $(\mathcal F_j)_{j\in J}$ of quasi-coherent modules of finite presentation, and compatible maps $\mathcal F_j\to\mathcal M$ exhibiting $\mathcal M$ as their colimit in all module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] with $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to view $X$ over the integers. Its small etale site and structure sheaf are identified with the original ones, hence the module category, quasi-coherence, finite presentations and the asserted colimit universal property are unchanged. The same atlas schemes and maps give the same point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], so quasi-compactness is unchanged; quasi-separatedness was already imposed on the absolute diagonal. Thus the hypotheses of absolute approximation apply.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-absolute-noetherian-approximation] to obtain a small nonempty directed set $I$, spaces $X_i$ with affine transitions, and $X\simeq\varprojlim_I X_i$, with every $X_i$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] to this system: its limit projections $q_i:X\to X_i$ are affine. Choose $i_0\in I$ using nonemptiness. We have obtained an affine morphism $q_{i_0}$ to a Noetherian algebraic space; no Noetherian property of $X$ has been inferred.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-noetherian-module-approximation] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, $f=q_{i_0}$, $Y=X_{i_0}$ and the given module $\mathcal M$. Step 2 supplies precisely affineness and Noetherianity of the target. The lemma supplies the small filtered diagram, its finitely presented quasi-coherent terms and its colimit cocone in all module sheaves. Under the ringed-site identification of step 1 these are the required objects and maps on the original $X$ over $S$.
